questions.question: Land-use records (in India) are maintained by the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**land revenue department**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The land revenue department is responsible for maintaining land-use records in India.
 
• These records are crucial for the management and administration of land resources.
 
• The department ensures the accurate documentation of land ownership, usage, and categorization.
 
• Land-use records assist in planning and implementing land-related policies and schemes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Land Revenue Act:**

 
 
• The act governs the maintenance of land records and administration of land revenue in India.
 
• It provides the legal framework for the collection of land revenue and management of land resources.
 
 
 
• **Digital Land Records:**
 
 
• Many states in India are digitizing land records to improve transparency and accessibility.
 
• Digital land records help in reducing disputes and frauds related to land ownership.
 
 
 
• **Revenue Department Functions:**
 
 
• The department handles land surveys, settlement operations, and collection of land revenue.
 
• It also deals with land reforms and redistribution of land to the landless.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Accurate Land Records:**
 
 
• Accurate records are essential for effective land management and urban planning.
 
• They play a crucial role in the implementation of agricultural policies and rural development programs.

questions.question: When government gives financial help to production units for selling their products at lower prices fixed by the government, what is it called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2) Subsidy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A subsidy is a financial assistance provided by the government to individuals, businesses, or institutions to promote economic and social policies.
 
• Subsidies help make products and services more affordable by reducing their production costs and thereby lowering market prices.
 
• Government subsidies are often provided to essential sectors such as agriculture, energy, and education to stabilize prices and ensure the availability of crucial goods and services.
 
• Subsidies can take various forms, including direct cash payments, tax breaks, or price supports, and are aimed at achieving specific economic objectives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Minimum Support Price (MSP)**:

 
 
• MSP is the price at which the government purchases crops from farmers, regardless of the market price, to ensure they receive a minimum profit for their harvest.
 
• It is announced by the government before the sowing season based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
 
 
 
• **Tax Rebate**:
 
 
• A tax rebate is a refund on taxes when the tax liability is less than the taxes paid.
 
• It serves as a financial relief mechanism for taxpayers and can be issued in various forms, such as direct refunds or reductions in future tax liabilities.
 
 
 
• **Discount**:
 
 
• A discount is a reduction in the price of goods or services, usually offered by sellers to attract customers or clear out stock.
 
• Unlike subsidies, discounts are provided directly by businesses rather than the government.
 
 
 
• **Price Controls**:
 
 
• Price controls are regulatory measures implemented by the government to set maximum or minimum prices for specific goods and services.
 
• These controls aim to prevent inflation, protect consumers, and ensure affordability of essential commodities.

questions.question:
Which of the following two rivers make 'estuaries'?

a) Narmada

b) Krishna

c) Cauvery

d) Tapi
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**d-a**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narmada River**:

 
 
• The Narmada River flows westwards and creates an estuary as it meets the Arabian Sea near Bharuch in Gujarat.
 
• It is one of the major rivers in central India, flowing through Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
 
• Estuaries are formed where the river meets the sea, mixing fresh and saltwater.
 
 
 
• **Tapi River**:
 
 
• The Tapi River also flows westwards and forms an estuary as it meets the Arabian Sea near Surat in Gujarat.
 
• It is another significant river in central India, flowing through Maharashtra and Gujarat.
 
• Like the Narmada, it mixes fresh and saltwater at its estuary.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Estuary**:

 
 
• An estuary is a coastal area where freshwater from rivers and streams meets and mixes with saltwater from the ocean.
 
• Estuaries are highly productive ecosystems, providing habitat for a wide variety of marine life.
 
• They often act as nurseries for many marine species, including fish and shellfish.
 
 
 
• **Westward-flowing Rivers in India**:
 
 
• Besides Narmada and Tapi, other westward-flowing rivers include Sabarmati and Mahi.
 
• These rivers generally flow towards the Arabian Sea.
 
 
 
• **River Mouth**:
 
 
• The mouth of a river is the part where it flows into another water body, such as an ocean, sea, or lake.
 
• River mouths can form various structures, including estuaries, deltas, and rias.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Estuary and Delta**:
 
 
• An estuary is formed by the mixing of river and sea water, while a delta is formed by sediment deposition at the river mouth.
 
• Deltas often have fertile land and support agriculture, whereas estuaries are more saline and support different types of ecosystems.

questions.question: What is a transfer income?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unearned income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Transfer income** refers to income received without providing any goods or services in return.
 
• This type of income typically includes **welfare payments, social security benefits, and other government subsidies**.
 
• It is termed **unearned income** as it is not earned through active employment or business activities.
 
• Examples include **pensions, unemployment benefits, and child support payments**.
 
• Transfer incomes are primarily aimed at **supporting individuals and households** in financial need.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earned Income**: Income derived from active work such as salaries, wages, and business profits.
 
• **Disposable Income**: The amount of money left to spend or save after taxes have been deducted from earnings.
 
• **Public Income**: Revenue collected by the government from various sources like taxes, fees, and public enterprises.
 
• **Unearned Income**: Includes transfer incomes, interest, dividends, and other forms of income not resulting from labor or business activities.
 
• Transfer payments are a significant part of **fiscal policy**, used to redistribute wealth and provide financial stability to vulnerable populations.

questions.question: Which state celebrated the 44th Kokborok Day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tripura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 44th Kokborok Day was celebrated by the state of **Tripura**.
 
• Kokborok Day is observed on **January 19th** every year to commemorate the recognition of Kokborok as an official language in Tripura in 1979.
 
• Kokborok is the native language of the **Tripuri people** of Tripura.
 
• The day is celebrated with cultural programs, literary events, and various activities to promote the language and its heritage.
 
• This celebration plays a significant role in preserving and promoting the **indigenous culture and traditions** of the Tripuri community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kokborok Language**:

 
 
• Kokborok, also known as Tripuri or Tiprakok, is a Tibeto-Burman language spoken primarily in the Indian state of Tripura.
 
• It is one of the official languages of Tripura, alongside Bengali and English.
 
• The language has its own script, known as the Kokborok script, but is also written in the Bengali and Latin scripts.
 
• Efforts are ongoing to develop and promote Kokborok through educational institutions and cultural activities.
 
 
 
• **Tripura**:
 
 
• Tripura is a state in northeastern India, bordered by Bangladesh to the north, south, and west.
 
• It is the third smallest state in India by area and has a rich cultural heritage with diverse ethnic communities.
 
• The state capital is Agartala, which is also the largest city in Tripura.
 
• Tripura is known for its beautiful landscapes, historical sites, and vibrant cultural festivals.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Communities of Tripura**:
 
 
• Tripura is home to several indigenous communities, including the Tripuri, Reang, Jamatia, Noatia, and Chakma.
 
• These communities have distinct languages, cultures, and traditions that contribute to the state's cultural diversity.
 
• The Tripuri people are the largest indigenous community in Tripura, and Kokborok is their native language.
 
• Indigenous festivals, such as Garia Puja and Kharchi Puja, are celebrated with great enthusiasm in Tripura.

questions.question: From which of the following countries the Asia Cup 2022 was shifted out to the United Arab Emirates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Asia Cup 2022 was originally scheduled to be hosted by Sri Lanka.
 
• Due to the economic and political crisis in Sri Lanka, the tournament was shifted to the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
 
• The decision to move the tournament was made to ensure the smooth and safe conduct of the matches.
 
• The UAE had previously hosted the Asia Cup in 2018, making it a familiar venue for the participating teams.
 
• The Asia Cup 2022 was held in the T20 format to serve as preparation for the ICC T20 World Cup.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic and Political Crisis in Sri Lanka:**

 
 
• Sri Lanka faced a severe economic crisis marked by shortages of essential items such as fuel, food, and medicines.
 
• Political instability further exacerbated the situation, leading to widespread protests and changes in government leadership.
 
• The crisis impacted various sectors, including tourism and sports, making it challenging to host international events.
 
 
 
• **UAE as a Cricket Venue:**
 
 
• The UAE is known for its state-of-the-art cricket infrastructure, including stadiums in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, and Sharjah.
 
• It has hosted several major cricket tournaments, including the IPL and previous editions of the Asia Cup.
 
• The country's neutral venue status often attracts international cricket matches.
 
 
 
• **Asia Cup Overview:**
 
 
• The Asia Cup is a men's One Day International and Twenty20 International cricket tournament.
 
• It was established in 1983 by the Asian Cricket Council to promote goodwill among Asian countries.
 
• India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan are the primary participating nations.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Teams:**
 
 
• Shifting the tournament to the UAE provided a neutral ground for all participating teams.
 
• Teams had to adapt to the hot and humid conditions of the UAE, which can affect player performance and strategies.
 
• The change in venue also impacted logistical arrangements, including travel and accommodation plans for teams and officials.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Stupa?

options.text: It is a holy place related with Jainism
This may contain things used by the Buddha or his followers
This may contain bodily remains of the Buddha or his followers
It means 'mound', whether round and tall, big and small

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a holy place related with Jainism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Stupas are primarily associated with Buddhism** and not Jainism.
 
• They were originally built to house the relics of the Buddha and his disciples.
 
• Stupas serve as a place for meditation and worship for Buddhists.
 
• The term 'stupa' means 'mound,' indicating its shape, which can vary in size and style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stupa Structure:**

 
 
• A stupa typically consists of a dome (anda), a base (medhi), and a spire (chatra).
 
• The anda symbolizes the universe, the medhi represents the earth, and the chatra signifies the heavens.
 
 
 
• **Types of Stupas:**
 
 
• Relic Stupas: Contain relics of the Buddha or his disciples.
 
• Object Stupas: Contain objects associated with the Buddha.
 
• Commemorative Stupas: Built to commemorate important events in the life of the Buddha or his disciples.
 
 
 
• **Famous Stupas:**
 
 
• The Great Stupa at Sanchi, India, is one of the oldest and most renowned stupas.
 
• The Shwedagon Pagoda in Myanmar and the Boudhanath Stupa in Nepal are other prominent examples.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Stupas are often seen as symbols of enlightenment and the path to Nirvana in Buddhism.
 
• They play a crucial role in the cultural and religious heritage of Buddhist communities worldwide.

questions.question: Which of the following leaders declared the creation of the People's Republic of China (PRC) in 1949?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mao Zedong**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mao Zedong**, also known as Chairman Mao, declared the creation of the People's Republic of China (PRC) on **October 1, 1949**.
 
• The declaration was made at Tiananmen Square in Beijing, marking the end of a prolonged civil war between the Communist Party of China and the Nationalist Party (Kuomintang).
 
• Mao Zedong was the founding father of the PRC and served as its first Chairman until his death in 1976.
 
• The establishment of the PRC signaled the beginning of a new era of Communist rule in China, which brought significant social, economic, and political changes to the country.
 
• This event is annually commemorated as National Day in China.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chinese Civil War**

 
 
• The Chinese Civil War was fought between the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Nationalist Party (Kuomintang or KMT) from 1927 to 1949.
 
• Key battles included the Battle of Huaihai and the Battle of Pingjin, which were decisive in the Communist victory.
 
 
 
• **Great Leap Forward**
 
 
• Initiated by Mao Zedong in 1958, the Great Leap Forward aimed to rapidly transform China from an agrarian society into a socialist society through rapid industrialization and collectivization.
 
• The campaign led to widespread famine and is considered a significant failure, resulting in millions of deaths.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Revolution**
 
 
• Launched by Mao Zedong in 1966, the Cultural Revolution sought to preserve Chinese communism by purging remnants of capitalist and traditional elements from Chinese society.
 
• It led to severe political and social upheavals and lasted until Mao's death in 1976.
 
 
 
• **Founding Principles of PRC**
 
 
• The PRC was founded on principles of Marxism-Leninism and sought to establish a classless society.
 
• The state aimed to control the means of production and implement central planning to achieve economic and social goals.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Abolition of intermediaries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution primarily focused on increasing agricultural production through technological advancements.
 
• It involved the use of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides.
 
• Mechanized means of cultivation were introduced to enhance productivity and efficiency.
 
• Multiple cropping systems were promoted to maximize land use and crop yields.
 
• Abolition of intermediaries was not a component of the Green Revolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yielding Varieties (HYV) Seeds:**

 
 
• These seeds were developed to produce more grains per plant compared to traditional varieties.
 
• HYV seeds played a crucial role in significantly increasing crop production.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Fertilizers:**
 
 
• The use of chemical fertilizers was encouraged to replenish soil nutrients and improve crop yields.
 
• Fertilizers such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium were commonly used.
 
 
 
• **Pesticides:**
 
 
• Pesticides were used to protect crops from pests and diseases, ensuring higher agricultural productivity.
 
• The use of pesticides helped in reducing crop losses and improving overall yields.
 
 
 
• **Mechanization:**
 
 
• Mechanized farming equipment, such as tractors and harvesters, were introduced to reduce labor costs and increase efficiency.
 
• Mechanization helped in timely farming operations and better management of agricultural practices.

questions.question: Which training platform developed in 2018 by trauma surgeon Dr. Alex Young provided remote educational programmes around the world skills like the right way to wear personal protective equipment, administer treatment or ventilate a patient during COVID-19?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**VIRTI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Virti** was developed in **2018** by trauma surgeon Dr. Alex Young.
 
• Virti provides **remote educational programmes** globally, focusing on crucial skills such as wearing personal protective equipment (PPE), administering treatment, and ventilating patients.
 
• It leverages **virtual reality (VR) and artificial intelligence (AI)** to enhance the training experience.
 
• Virti became especially relevant during the **COVID-19 pandemic**, aiding healthcare workers in managing the crisis effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Virtual Reality (VR) in Healthcare**

 
 
• VR technology simulates real-life scenarios, providing immersive training experiences for medical professionals.
 
• It helps in procedural training, anatomy learning, and patient interaction simulations.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Medical Training**
 
 
• AI enhances personalized learning by adapting training modules to individual needs.
 
• It provides real-time feedback and analytics to improve performance.
 
 
 
• **Importance of PPE Training**
 
 
• Proper use of PPE is crucial to prevent infection spread, especially during pandemics.
 
• Training ensures that healthcare workers are protected and can safely treat patients.
 
 
 
• **Impact of COVID-19 on Medical Training**
 
 
• The pandemic necessitated remote and virtual training solutions due to social distancing measures.
 
• Platforms like Virti became essential for continuous professional development and skill enhancement.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India grants protection to persons who are arrested or detained?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 22** of the Indian Constitution provides specific rights and protections to individuals who are arrested or detained.
 
• It ensures that no person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed of the grounds for such arrest.
 
• Article 22 guarantees the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of their choice.
 
• It mandates that an arrested person must be produced before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours of arrest, excluding the time necessary for the journey to the magistrate's court.
 
• The article also lays down provisions regarding preventive detention, specifying the maximum period of detention and the procedural safeguards that must be followed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Preventive Detention**:

 
 
• Preventive detention refers to the act of detaining an individual to prevent them from committing a future crime.
 
• Under Article 22, a person can be detained without trial for a maximum period of three months unless an Advisory Board reports sufficient cause for extended detention.
 
 
 
• **Protection against Arbitrary Arrest**:
 
 
• Article 22 provides protection against arbitrary arrest and detention, ensuring that individuals are informed of the reasons for their arrest and have the right to legal representation.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**:
 
 
• Article 22 is part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution, which guarantees civil liberties to individuals to ensure their protection and freedom.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review**:
 
 
• The provisions under Article 22 are subject to judicial review, ensuring that any misuse of power by the authorities can be challenged in the courts.

questions.question: Which is the first tomb of the Mughal period to have two domes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun Tomb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Humayun's Tomb, located in Delhi, is the first garden-tomb in India and a significant example of Mughal architecture.
 
• It was commissioned by Humayun's widow, Empress Bega Begum (Hajji Begum), in 1569-70, and designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas.
 
• The tomb is known for its double dome, a structural innovation that became a hallmark of Mughal architecture.
 
• The double dome technique consists of an outer layer that rises high for aesthetic grandeur and an inner layer that maintains the correct proportions inside.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Architecture**

 
 
• It is a unique blend of Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.
 
• Mughal architecture is known for its symmetrical and decorative elements, including elaborate gardens, massive domes, and intricate carvings.
 
 
 
• **Double Dome**
 
 
• A double dome consists of two layers: an outer shell for height and grandeur, and an inner shell for a proportionate interior.
 
• This technique ensures that the interior space is aesthetically pleasing and structurally sound.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India**
 
 
• Humayun's Tomb was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.
 
• India has several UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including the Taj Mahal, Qutub Minar, and Red Fort.
 
 
 
• **Garden Tomb**
 
 
• Humayun's Tomb is considered the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The garden layout is known as Char Bagh, a Persian-style quadrilateral garden divided by walkways or flowing water into four smaller parts.

questions.question: According to Niti Aayog's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021, which state of India has the lowest percentage of population below poverty line?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Niti Aayog's Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021, Kerala has the lowest percentage of population below the poverty line.
 
• Kerala's poverty rate stands at 0.71%, the lowest among Indian states.
 
• The index measures multiple deprivations faced by individuals in their daily lives, including health, education, and standard of living.
 
• Kerala's high human development indicators, such as literacy rate and life expectancy, contribute to its low poverty rate.
 
• Effective implementation of social welfare schemes and high public health standards are significant factors in reducing poverty in Kerala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• The MPI is an international measure of acute poverty, accounting for various deprivations in health, education, and living standards.
 
• It was developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI).
 
• The MPI complements traditional income-based poverty measures.
 
• It helps in identifying the most vulnerable people and understanding the intensity of poverty.
 
 
 
• **Human Development Indicators (HDIs):**
 
 
• HDIs are statistical tools used to measure a country's overall achievement in its social and economic dimensions.
 
• These indicators include life expectancy, education level, and per capita income.
 
• Kerala ranks high in HDIs due to its effective social policies and investment in public health and education.
 
 
 
• **Social Welfare Schemes in Kerala:**
 
 
• Kerala has implemented various welfare schemes such as the Kudumbashree mission for women's empowerment and social development.
 
• Other programs include comprehensive health insurance schemes and subsidized food distribution systems.
 
 
 
• **Public Health Standards in Kerala:**
 
 
• Kerala's public health system is one of the best in India, with accessible and affordable healthcare services.
 
• High literacy rates contribute to better health awareness and practices among the population.

questions.question: What was the role of "Bakshi" under Mughal Central Administration?

options.text: He was responsible for keeping strict watch over proper maintenance of the sanctioned size of armed contingents and war equipage by the mansabdars.
He was the chief executive officer responsible for the purchase of all kinds of articles and their storage for the royal household.
He had unlimited authority to distribute allowances and stipends to all other ranks and officers of administration.
He was responsible for revenue and finances and his primary duty was to supervise the imperial treasury and check all accounts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**He was responsible for keeping strict watch over proper maintenance of the sanctioned size of armed contingents and war equipage by the mansabdars.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bakshi was a high-ranking official in the Mughal military administration.
 
• His primary role was to ensure that the mansabdars maintained their assigned military contingents and war equipment according to their rank.
 
• He monitored the muster rolls and inspected the troops to verify the actual number of soldiers and equipment.
 
• The Bakshi also played a crucial role in organizing the logistics for military campaigns, including the supply of provisions and weapons.
 
• He reported directly to the emperor and was a key figure in maintaining the efficiency and readiness of the Mughal army.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mansabdari System:**

 
 
• Introduced by Akbar, the Mansabdari system was a bureaucratic structure for managing the nobility and the military.
 
• Mansabdars were ranked officials who were assigned a specific number of troops and responsibilities.
 
• Ranks ranged from 10 to 10,000, and higher ranks were associated with greater responsibilities and privileges.
 
• Mansabdars were paid through revenue assignments called jagirs.
 
 
 
• **Diwan-i-Wazarat:**
 
 
• The Diwan-i-Wazarat was responsible for revenue and finances in the Mughal administration.
 
• This department supervised the collection of taxes and managed the imperial treasury.
 
• The head of the Diwan-i-Wazarat was known as the Wazir or the Diwan.
 
 
 
• **Mir Bakshi:**
 
 
• The Mir Bakshi was another key official in the Mughal military administration.
 
• He was responsible for the administration of the military payroll and the assignment of jagirs to the mansabdars.
 
• The Mir Bakshi also managed the recruitment and training of soldiers.
 
 
 
• **Imperial Military Structure:**
 
 
• The Mughal military was a well-organized force with a hierarchical structure.
 
• It included various regiments such as infantry, cavalry, artillery, and elephant corps.
 
• The military hierarchy ensured efficient command and control during campaigns.

questions.question: Which of the following is a religious festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Gangaur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gangaur** is a major festival celebrated in the Indian state of Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and West Bengal.
 
• This festival is dedicated to **Goddess Gauri (Parvati)**, the consort of Lord Shiva, and symbolizes marital bliss and the harvest season.
 
• Gangaur is celebrated with great enthusiasm and traditional rituals, including the worship of clay idols of Gauri and Isar (Shiva).
 
• The festival lasts for 16 days, starting from the first day of Chaitra (March-April) and ending on the third day of Shukla Paksha in the same month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Children's Day** is celebrated on November 14th in India to mark the birth anniversary of the first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• The **Camel Festival** is an annual event held in Bikaner, Rajasthan, celebrating the significance of camels in the region.
 
• **Teachers' Day** in India is celebrated on September 5th, commemorating the birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, a philosopher and statesman.
 
• **Religious Festivals**: These are events celebrated by various religious communities to honor deities, prophets, or significant religious events, often involving rituals, prayers, and cultural activities.

questions.question: In the month of September 2022, the Prime Minister of which of the following countries visited the dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti at Ajmer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In September 2022, the Prime Minister of Bangladesh, Sheikh Hasina, visited the dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti at Ajmer, India.
 
• Sheikh Hasina's visit was part of a broader diplomatic trip to India aimed at strengthening bilateral relations between the two nations.
 
• The dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti, a revered Sufi saint, is located in Ajmer, Rajasthan, and is a significant religious site attracting visitors from around the world.
 
• The visit underscored the cultural and historical ties shared between India and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sheikh Hasina:**

 
 
• Sheikh Hasina is the current Prime Minister of Bangladesh, serving since January 2009.
 
• She is the daughter of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the founding leader of Bangladesh.
 
• Her leadership has seen significant economic growth and development in Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti:**
 
 
• Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti, also known as Gharib Nawaz, was a prominent Sufi saint of the Chishti Order in India.
 
• His teachings emphasized love, tolerance, and openness, making his dargah a site of pilgrimage for people of various faiths.
 
 
 
• **India-Bangladesh Relations:**
 
 
• India and Bangladesh share a long history of cultural, economic, and political ties.
 
• The two countries cooperate on various issues, including trade, security, and regional stability.
 
 
 
• **Sufi Tradition:**
 
 
• Sufism is a mystical form of Islam that emphasizes the inward search for God and the cultivation of spiritual closeness to Him.
 
• Sufi saints, like Khwaja Moinuddin Chisti, played a key role in spreading the message of Islam in South Asia through their teachings and personal example.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian classical dance forms is known to be 'ekaharya'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bharatnatyam** is a major Indian classical dance form that originated in the **Tamil Nadu** region.
 
• The term **'ekaharya'** in Bharatnatyam refers to the **solo performance** of multiple roles by a single dancer.
 
• Bharatnatyam is characterized by **expressive hand gestures (mudras), intricate footwork, and facial expressions**.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in **spiritual themes** and is often performed as an offering to deities in temples.
 
• Bharatnatyam involves a combination of **Nritya (expressive dance) and Nritta (pure dance)** elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abhinaya**: Refers to the art of expression in Indian classical dance, involving facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements.
 
• **Natya Shastra**: An ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts written by Bharata Muni, which serves as the foundational text for Bharatnatyam.
 
• **Arangetram**: The debut performance of a Bharatanatyam dancer, marking their transition from student to professional performer.
 
• **Varnam**: A central piece in a Bharatnatyam repertoire, typically showcasing the dancer's technical prowess and expressive abilities.
 
• **Adavus**: Basic units of movement in Bharatnatyam, combining footwork, hand gestures, and body movements.

questions.question: In October 2021, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommended RTS,S/AS01 (RTS,S), for use in children at risk in sub-Saharan Africa and in other regions with moderate to high transmission of which disease caused by Plasmodium falciparum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malaria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In October 2021, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommended the RTS,S/AS01 (RTS,S) malaria vaccine for children at risk in sub-Saharan Africa and in other regions with moderate to high transmission of malaria.
 
• RTS,S/AS01, also known as Mosquirix, is the first and only vaccine shown to significantly reduce malaria and life-threatening severe malaria in young children.
 
• The recommendation is based on results from an ongoing pilot programme in Ghana, Kenya, and Malawi that has reached more than 800,000 children since 2019.
 
• Malaria is caused by the Plasmodium parasite, with Plasmodium falciparum being the most deadly species and the most prevalent in Africa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmodium falciparum:**

 
 
• It is the most dangerous of the malaria parasites that infect humans.
 
• It is responsible for the majority of malaria-related deaths globally.
 
• Transmission occurs through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.
 
 
 
• **World Health Organization (WHO):**
 
 
• WHO is a specialized agency of the United Nations responsible for international public health.
 
• It was established on 7 April 1948 and is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
 
• WHO plays a critical role in the coordination of global health responses and disease prevention strategies.
 
 
 
• **RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) Vaccine:**
 
 
• Developed by GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) in partnership with the PATH Malaria Vaccine Initiative.
 
• The vaccine works by triggering the immune system to defend against the first stages of malaria when the parasite enters the human host’s bloodstream through a mosquito bite.
 
• It is administered in a series of four doses in children from 5 months of age.
 
 
 
• **Global Malaria Burden:**
 
 
• In 2020, there were an estimated 241 million malaria cases and 627,000 malaria deaths worldwide.
 
• Approximately 95% of malaria cases and 96% of malaria deaths occur in the WHO African Region.
 
• Children under 5 years of age are the most vulnerable group affected by malaria.

questions.question:
The National population register was created under the provision of _________ and

a) Citizen Act 1965

b) Citizenship Rules 2004

c) Citizenship Act 1955

d) Citizenship Rules 2003
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1)c-d**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National Population Register (NPR) is linked to the **Citizenship Act 1955**.
 
• The NPR is governed by the rules laid out in the **Citizenship Rules 2003**.
 
• The NPR aims to create a comprehensive identity database of every usual resident in the country.
 
• It includes both demographic and biometric details of the individuals.
 
• The NPR is prepared at the local (village/sub-town), sub-district, district, state, and national level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Act 1955**:

 
 
• This Act provides the provisions for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship.
 
• It has been amended several times to address various aspects of citizenship.
 
 
 
• **Citizenship Rules 2003**:
 
 
• The rules were framed to facilitate the implementation of the Citizenship Act 1955.
 
• They include provisions for the registration of citizens and the issuance of national identity cards.
 
 
 
• **National Population Register (NPR)**:
 
 
• The NPR is a comprehensive database of all usual residents in India.
 
• It is mandatory for every usual resident to register in the NPR.
 
 
 
• **Demographic and Biometric Data**:
 
 
• Demographic data includes details like name, date of birth, gender, and marital status.
 
• Biometric data includes fingerprints and iris scans.
